bull.b: Sustained ARR and a rapidly rising SaaS mix create durable recurring revenue. Strong SaaS growth and a high share of net new ARR increase predictability, improve unit economics long-term, and support upsell/expansion strategies that compound revenue over multiple years.

Improving adjusted margins and a clear swing to positive operating and free cash flow indicate the business is converting revenue into sustainable cash. Better cash generation supports reinvestment in product, GTM, and potential buybacks or debt reduction over a multi-quarter horizon.

bull.t: Stronger Balance Sheet / Low Leverage in 2026
bull.b: Material improvement in leverage and a high equity cushion provide financial flexibility to fund growth, absorb shocks, and pursue strategic initiatives. Low current debt levels reduce refinancing risk and allow management to prioritize R&D and SaaS migration investments.

bear.b: Despite top-line growth and gross margin stability, the company still posts sizable net and operating losses. Prolonged negative profitability risks cash runway pressure and requires sustained margin expansion and scale to prove earnings durability and free-cash-flow consistency.

Prior years' negative equity and elevated debt highlight capital-structure instability. That history raises refinancing and execution risk during downturns, and means improvements must be sustained to rebuild investor confidence and guard against recurrence under stress.

bear.t: Execution Risk: Migrations & Early Agentic Monetization
bear.b: Future SaaS expansion depends on executing migrations and monetizing new Agentic products. Both are early-stage and timing-sensitive; slower migrations or delayed Agentic revenue would weaken projected SaaS growth, margin improvement, and the durability of the recent cash-flow turnaround.
